21879.text: Three houses are available in a locality. Three persons apply for the houses. Each applies for one house without consulting others. The probability that all three apply for the same house is
21879.sol: Each of the three persons can apply for any of the three houses. Since each person has 3 choices, the total number of ways for three persons to apply for the houses is 3 3 3 = 3^3 = 27 . For all three persons to apply for the same house, they must all choose house 1, or all choose house 2, or all choose house 3. There are 3 such favorable outcomes. The probability is the ratio of the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes: P = 3 27 = 1 9 Answer: 1 9

55904.text: Which of the following is correct decreasing order of the repulsive interaction of electron pairs in a molecule?
options: lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair
bond pair-bond pair = bond pair-lone pair > lone pair-lone pair
lone pair-bond pair > lone pair-lone pair > bond pair-bond pair
bond pair-bond pair > lone pair-bond pair > lone pair-lone pair
55904.sol: In a molecule, the correct decreasing order of the repulsive interectlon of electron pairs is, lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair. Two atoms share bond pairs of electrons, whereas the lone pair of electrons is only influenced by the central atom. 82035.text: Position of non-polar and polar parts in micelle is:

polar at the inner surface but nonpolar at the outer surface
are present in the surface only
82035.sol: Micelles are the clusters formed by the association of colloids. They are formed by lyophilic and lyophobic groups. As the concentration increases, the lyophobic parts receding away from the solvent approach each (non-polar part) other and form a cluster, the lyophobic ends are in the interior, lyophilic groups (polar part) projecting outward in contact with the solvent. In a non-polar solvent, the hydrophilic groups are sequestered in the micelle core and the hydrophobic groups extend away from the centre.

84411.sol: In salamander, mesonephric kidney are the excretory organs, and excrete urea. In labeo (rohu), mesonephric kidney are the excretory organs, and excrete ammonia. 84416.text: A fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) activates
options: juxta glomerular cells to release renin
84416.sol: Juxtaglomerular apparatus consists of macula densa and juxtaglomerular cells. The apparatus becomes active when there is decrease in renal blood pressure or decrease in glomerular filtration rate. There is increased absorption of NaCl in ascending limb or loop of Henle. The decreased NaCl content of filtrate activates cells of macula densa to increase secretion of renin from juxta glomerular cells. Renin convert angiotensinogen to angiotensin peptides.

84468.subject: Zoology
84468.text: The yellowish fluid "colostrum" secreted by mammary glands of mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant antibodies ( IgA ) to protect the infant. This type of immunity is called as:
84468.sol: Immunity is said to be passive when antibodies produced in other organisms are injected into a person to counteract antigens such as snake venom. The yellowish fluid ‘colostrum’ secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation is a form of natural passive immunity. It has plenty of antibodies ( IgA ) to protect the infant during the initial months of life. Maternal antibodies ( IgG ) are also transmitted through the placenta. Such an immunity is called natural passive immunity.

84516.subject: Zoology

84516.sol: ELISA (Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay), also known as an enzyme immunoassay (EIA), is a biochemical technique used mainly in immunology to detect the presence of an antibody or an antigen in a sample. It is a useful tool for determining serum antibody concentrations (such as with the HIV test). The ELISA was the first screning test widely used for HIV because of its high sensitivity.

Menstruation - Breakdown of myometrium and ovum
84670.sol: In secretory phase during ovulation, the follicle breaks and collapses under the continuous influence of Luteinizing Hormone (LH). It begins to enlarge and forms a yellowish structure, called the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum plays an important role in the preparation of the endometrium for the implantation of the fertilized egg by secreting estrogens and progesterone.

122753.sol: Gynoecium is the female reproductive part of the flower and is made up of one or more carpels. A carpel consists of three parts namely stigma, style and ovary. Ovary is the enlarged basal part, on which lies the elongated tube, the style. The style connects the ovary to the stigma. The stigma is usually at the tip of the style and is the receptive surface for pollen grains. Each ovary bears one or more ovules attached to a flattened, cushion-like placenta. When more than one carpel is present, they may be free (as

124769.sol: The cells that lose their protoplasm and develop strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to carry water under extreme tension are the tracheary elements (tracheids and vessels) of the xylem. The process by which cells derived from root apical and shoot apical meristems and cambium mature to perform specific functions is called differentiation. 124984.sol: The TCA cycle starts with the condensation of acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid (OAA) and water to yield citric acid (Figure 12.3). The reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme citrate synthase and a molecule of CoA is released. Citrate is then isomerized to isocitrate. It is followed by two successive steps of decarboxylation, leading to the formation of α-ketoglutaric acid

The primary CO₂ acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule, Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP), and the enzyme responsible for catalyzing this carboxylation is PEP carboxylase (PEPcase). 125664.sol: Photosystem II (PS II) has an absorption maximum at 680 nm , while Photosystem I (PS I) has an absorption maximum at 700 nm . When only PS I is functional, the excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain. 128251.subject: Zoology
128251.text: Number of cranial nerves in frog :
128251.sol: Ten pairs of cranial nerves are present in anamniotes such as fishes and amphibians (e.g., Frog). Twelve pairs of cranial nerves are present in amniotes, reptiles, birds and mammals including rabbit and humans.

128877.subject: Zoology

128877.sol: The entire heart is made of cardiac muscles. The walls of ventricles are much thicker than that of the atria. A specialised cardiac musculature called the nodal tissue is also distributed in the heart. A patch of this tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). Another mass of this tissue is seen in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum called the atrio-ventricular node (AVN ). A bundle of nodal fibres, atrioventricular

128962.subject: Zoology
128962.text: Identify the correct statement w.r.t given figure.
options: QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular diastole.
The P-wave represents the depolarisation of the atria, which leads to the contraction of the atrium.
The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from normal state to excited state.
The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole.
128962.sol: The P-wave represents the electrical excitation (or depolarisation) of the atria, which leads to the contraction of both the atria. The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole. The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from excited to normal state (repolarisation). The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole.

129243.subject: Zoology
129243.text: What is the function of the association areas in the brain?
129243.sol: A deep cleft divides the cerebrum longitudinally into two halves, which are called the left and right cerebral hemispheres. The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions, called the association areas, are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and communication. The cerebral cortex is referred to as the grey matter due to its greyish appearance as the neuron cell bodies are concent

129341.subject: Zoology
129341.text: During the initiation of muscle contraction, a neural signal triggers the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft. The specific receptors for acetylcholine are located on the:
129341.sol: At the neuromuscular junction (motor end plate), the arrival of a neural signal causes the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine from the motor neuron into the synaptic cleft. Acetylcholine diffuses across the cleft and binds to its specific receptors, which are located on the sarcolemma (the plasma membrane of the muscle fibre). This binding generates an action potential in the sarcolemma that spreads through the muscle fibre. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the internal storehouse for calcium ions. Synaptic

129612.subject: Zoology

The above described transport of substances facilitated by the special arrangement of Henle’s loop and vasa recta is called the counter current mechanism. This mechanism helps to maintain a concentration gradient in the medullary interstitium.

130405.sol: True Ribs: The first 7 pairs, directly attached to the sternum via costal cartilage. Costal Cartilage: Connects the ribs to the sternum, providing flexibility.

RNA has an additional –OH group present at 2'-position in the ribose
DNA has an additional –OH group present at 2'-position in the ribose
DNA has uracil in place of thymine

DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it ‘Nuclein’. They are toxic and harmful to the environment and to human beings and animals

133800.sol: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. These chemicals are toxic and extremely harmful, to human beings and animals alike, and have been polluting our environment (soil, ground water), fruits, vegetables and crop plants. The value 95 mm Hg represents the pumping pressure of the heart.
Prolonged occurrence of this condition can adversely affect vital organs like the brain and kidney.
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a09.sol: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. A repeated measurement of 150/95 mm Hg indicates hypertension (high blood pressure). 95295.subject: Botany
95295.text: All of the following statements are incorrect about a monocot stem, except
options: hypodermis of monocot stem is made up of multiple layers of parenchyma
vascular bundles are surrounded by sclerenchymatous bundle sheath .
the vascular cylinder is surrounded by a parenchymatous pericycle in monocot stem
peripheral vascular bundles are generally larger than the centrally located ones.
95295.sol: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. It doesn't have pericycle. Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

95518.subject: Botany
95518.text: Read the following matches about chordates and it's characteristics. I. Petromyzon- belongs to Cyclostomata and are endoparasites on some fishes. II. Scoliodon- a Chondrichthyes in which teeth are modified placoid scales. III. Hippocampus- a cartilaginous aquarium fish known as a sea horse. IV. Ichthyophis is a limbless viviparous amphibian with direct development. Select the incorrect statements?
95518.sol: Petromyzon- belongs to cyclostomata and are ectoparasites on some fishes. Hippocampus- a bony non-aquarium fish known as sea horse. Ichthyophis is a limbless oviparous amphibian with indirect development. Scoliodon- a chondrichthyes in which teeth are modified placoid scales.

95949.subject: Botany
95949.text: In which group of fungi, conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores?
95949.sol: The asexual spores that are found on the external surface of the spore-producing structures or cells (conidiophores) which produces it are known as conidia. This kind of reproduction is seen in the ascomycetes group of fungi also known as sac fungi which are mostly multicellular saprophytic decomposers a parasitic. Few examples of this fungi are Penicillium, Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora.

95963.subject: Botany
95963.sol: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells is stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm, e.g., phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules. Gas vacuoles are found in blue-green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.

95988.subject: Botany
95988.text: Some of the enzymes, which are associated with the digestion of proteins, lipids and nucleic acids, are present in
95988.sol: The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases such as lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

96092.subject: Botany
96092.text: The basic structure of the cell membrane
options: is a lipid bilayer that serves as a barrier to water-soluble molecules.
is a lipid bilayer that serves as a barrier to lipid-soluble molecules.
is best described as lipids dispersed within a protein bilayer.
​is a protein bilayer that serves as a barrier to lipid-soluble molecules.
96092.sol: Plasma membrane or the cell membrane separates the inside environment of cell from the outside environment. It protects the cell from the exterior environment. The cell membrane is mainly made of proteins and phospholipids. The phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer pattern with the hydrophobic tail on the inside and the hydrophilic head towards the outside. This protects the tail from aqueous environment and serves as a barrier to water-soluble molecule. The proteins are found on the surface of the membrane and a

96094.subject: Botany
96094.text: A cell organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes is:
96094.sol: These are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

96291.subject: Botany
96291.sol: Syncytium means 'together' or 'fused'. It is multinucleate cell formed by formation of uninucleate cells. This is seen in plants too. Coconut contains liquid known as liquid endosperm. It is formed by free nuclear divisions without undergoing cytoplasmic division. Hence it is multinucleate or syncytium.

96318.subject: Botany
96318.text: Select the correct option for the following A The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases ...(i)... and ...(ii)... B During ...(iii).... cell is metabolically active and continuously grows. C Centroile duplicates in the cytoplasm during ....(iv)......
options: (i) Interphase (ii) M-phase (iii) G1 phase (iv) S phase
(i) G1 phase (ii) S-phase (iii) Interphase (iv) S phase
(i) Interphase (ii) M-phase (iii) G2 phase (iv) G1 phase
(i) Karyokinesis (ii) Cytokinesis (iii) G1 phase (iv) S phase
96318.sol: The cell cycle is divided into two phases interphase which is longer in duration than M-phase. Interphase consists of three subphases G1, S, and G2 phase. During the G1 phase cell is metabolically active and continuously grows. Duplication of centriole occurs during the S phase.

96510.subject: Botany
96510.text: Which of the following is correct about keystone species in an ecosystem?
options: The number is maximum in an ecosystem.
They aren't required in an ecosystem.
They have the largest biomass in an ecosystem.
They are main contributors to ecosystem properties
96510.sol: The keystone species in an ecosystem are those who are the main contributors to the ecosystem.

96790.subject: Botany
96790.text: The concentration of essential element below which plant growth is retarded is termed as:
96790.sol: A chemical nutrient that is necessary for plant growth and development is known as essential elements and they are 17 in number. Due to deficiency of it plants become unable to complete their life cycle. Critical concentration is the minimum concentration of mineral below that the plant growth will get retarded or stunted. If the concentration of the essential elements rises above the critical concentration then that leads to toxicity or the death of the plants.

97002.subject: Botany
97002.text: Among the members of the list given below, how many plants have superior ovary? China rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, guava, cucumber, onion and tulip.
97002.sol: A superior ovary is found in plants of china rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, onion and tulip.

97444.subject: Botany
97444.text: Which of the following belongs to Rhodophyta?
97444.sol: Polysiphonia is a species of red algae. Sphagnum includes members known as peat mosses. Polytrichum is a genus of the mosses which contain members commonly known as the hair mosses. Funaria are mosses belonging to the family Funariaceae.

97584.subject: Botany
options: Cytochromes are found in cristae of mitochondria
After glycolysis, fate of glucose in mitochondrial matrix is reduction
Net gain of ATP in aerobic respiration is 36 ATP
There is one step in Kreb's cycle where F A D + reduced to F A D H 2 .
97584.sol: After glycolysis, pyruvic acid formed in cytoplasm enters the mitochondrial matrix and undergoes oxidation which occurs by oxidative decarboxylation to release carbon dioxide, NADH 2 and form acetyl Co-A.

97903.subject: Botany
97903.text: Who from the following first proposed the natural system of classification?
97903.sol: The natural classification systems developed are based on the natural affinities among the organisms and considered, not only the external features but also internal features, like ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry. Such a classification of flowering plants was given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker.

98150.subject: Chemistry
98150.text: Which one is the cofactor of carboxypeptidase?
98150.sol: A number of enzymes require metal ions for their activity which form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate, e.g., zinc is a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase. Catalytic activity is lost when the co-factor is removed from the enzyme which testifies that they play a crucial role in the catalytic activity of the enzyme.

98168.subject: Chemistry
98168.text: The enzyme activity can be completely stopped by
options: Removing its product as fast as it is formed
98168.sol: An active site of an enzyme is a crevice or pocket into which the substrate fits. Thus, enzymes catalyze reactions at a high rate through their active site. Once the site is blocked, the enzyme-substrate reaction is stopped, as the substrate cannot complete the reaction without forming its complex with the enzyme at the active site.

Both T l 3 + and A l 3 + ions act as oxidizing agent in aqueous solution.
Hydrogen bonding in H 3 B O 3 gives it a layered structure.
B ( O E t ) 3 imparts blue colour to the burner flame.

98879.subject: Chemistry
98879.text: Which one of the following arrangement of molecules is correct on the basis of their dipole moments?
options: B F 3 > N H 3 > N F 3
B F 3 > N F 3 > N H 3
N H 3 > B F 3 > N F 3
N H 3 > N F 3 > B F 3
98879.sol: Both N F 3 and N H 3 have identical shape (pyramidal) and a lone pair of electron on nitrogen. Dipole moment of N H 3 is higher than N F 3 molecule as the orbital moment due to lone pair of electrons and the resultant dipole moment of 3 N-F bonds point in the opposite directions to that of lone pair of electrons. B F 3 is a symmetrical molecule. It has zero dipole moment.

in neither DC nor AC circuits
306394.sol: A transformer operates on the principle of mutual induction, which requires a continuously changing magnetic flux to induce an electromotive force (EMF) in the secondary coil. In an AC circuit, the alternating current produces a varying magnetic field, allowing the transformer to function. In a DC circuit, the steady current produces a constant magnetic field, resulting in zero induced EMF in the secondary coil. Therefore, transformers are employed solely in AC circuits.

6a7a1ff88c86ae59852d0fc3.text: Let the vertex A of an isosceles triangle ABC ( AB = AC ) be (8, 1, 1) . The base BC lies on the line x-2 2 = y+1 3 = z-4 6 . If the area of ABC is 49 sq. units, then the sum of the squares of the coordinates of the vertices B and C is _______.
6a7a1ff88c86ae59852d0fc3.sol: Let the given line be L: x-2 2 = y+1 3 = z-4 6 = . Any point on L is of the form P(2 +2, 3 -1, 6 +4) . If P is the foot of the perpendicular from A(8, 1, 1) to L , then the direction ratios of AP are (2 -6, 3 -2, 6 +3) . Since AP is perpendicular to L , we have: 2(2 -6) + 3(3 -2) + 6(6 +3) = 0 4 - 12 + 9 - 6 + 36 + 18 = 0 49 = 0 = 0 . So, the foot of the perpendicular is P(2, -1, 4) .
